title: Proverbs, Chapter 28 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 28 on folios 419r, 419v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 28 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 419r, 419v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>נָ֣סוּ וְאֵין־רֹדֵ֣ף רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים כִּכְפִ֥יר יִבְטָֽח׃ <sup>2</sup>בְּפֶ֣שַֽׁע אֶ֭רֶץ רַבִּ֣ים שָׂרֶ֑יהָ וּבְאָדָ֥ם מֵבִ֥ין יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ כֵּ֣ן יַאֲרִֽיךְ׃ <sup>3</sup>גּבֶר רָ֭שׁ וְעֹשֵׁ֣ק דַּלִּ֑ים מָטָ֥ר סֹ֝חֵ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין לָֽחֶם׃ <sup>4</sup>עֹזְבֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָה יְהַֽלְל֣וּ רָשָׁ֑ע וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י ת֝וֹרָ֗ה יִתְגָּ֥רוּ בָֽם׃ פ <sup>5</sup>אַנְשֵׁי־רָ֭ע לֹא־יָבִ֣ינוּ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָבִ֥ינוּ כֹֽל׃ <sup>6</sup>טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם וְה֣וּא עָשִֽׁיר׃ <sup>7</sup>נוֹצֵ֣ר תּ֭וֹרָה בֵּ֣ן מֵבִ֑ין וְרֹעֶ֥ה זֽ֝וֹלְלִ֗ים יַכְלִ֥ים אָבִֽיו׃ <sup>8</sup>מַרְבֶּ֣ה ה֭וֹנוֹ בְּנֶ֣שֶׁךְ ובתרבית [וְתַרְבִּ֑ית] לְחוֹנֵ֖ן דַּלִּ֣ים יִקְבְּצֶֽנּוּ׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion. <sup>2</sup>For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged. <sup>3</sup>A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food. <sup>4</sup>They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them. <sup>5</sup>Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things. <sup>6</sup>Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich. <sup>7</sup>Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father. <sup>8</sup>He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>מֵסִ֣יר אָ֭זְנוֹ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ תּוֹרָ֑ה גַּ֥ם תְּ֝פִלָּת֗וֹ תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃ <sup>10</sup>מַשְׁגֶּ֤ה יְשָׁרִ֨ים ׀ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ רָ֗ע בִּשְׁחוּת֥וֹ הֽוּא־יִפּ֑וֹל וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִנְחֲלוּ־טֽוֹב׃ <sup>11</sup>חָכָ֣ם בְּ֭עֵינָיו אִ֣ישׁ עָשִׁ֑יר וְדַ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין יַחְקְרֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>12</sup>בַּעֲלֹ֣ץ צַ֭דִּיקִים רַבָּ֣ה תִפְאָ֑רֶת וּבְק֥וּם רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְחֻפַּ֥שׂ אָדָֽם׃ <sup>13</sup>מְכַסֶּ֣ה פְ֭שָׁעָיו לֹ֣א יַצְלִ֑יחַ וּמוֹדֶ֖ה וְעֹזֵ֣ב יְרֻחָֽם׃ <sup>14</sup>אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃ <sup>15</sup>אֲרִי־נֹ֭הֵם וְדֹ֣ב שׁוֹקֵ֑ק מֹשֵׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע עַ֣ל עַם־דָּֽל׃ <sup>16</sup>נָגִ֗יד חֲסַ֣ר תְּ֭בוּנוֹת וְרַ֥ב מַעֲשַׁקּ֑וֹת שנאי [שֹׂ֥נֵא] בֶ֝֗צַע יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִֽים׃ פ
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination. <sup>10</sup>Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession. <sup>11</sup>The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out. <sup>12</sup>When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden. <sup>13</sup>He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. <sup>14</sup>Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. <sup>15</sup>As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people. <sup>16</sup>The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>אָ֭דָם עָשֻׁ֣ק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ עַד־בּ֥וֹר יָ֝נ֗וּס אַל־יִתְמְכוּ־בֽוֹ׃ <sup>18</sup>הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים יִוָּשֵׁ֑עַ וְנֶעְקַ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם יִפּ֥וֹל בְּאֶחָֽת׃ <sup>19</sup>עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֥ף רֵ֝קִ֗ים יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־רִֽישׁ׃ <sup>20</sup>אִ֣ישׁ אֱ֭מוּנוֹת רַב־בְּרָכ֑וֹת וְאָ֥ץ לְ֝הַעֲשִׁ֗יר לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃ <sup>21</sup>הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֥ים לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְעַל־פַּת־לֶ֝֗חֶם יִפְשַׁע־גָּֽבֶר׃ <sup>22</sup>נִֽבֳהָֽל לַה֗וֹן אִ֭ישׁ רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝דַע כִּי־חֶ֥סֶר יְבֹאֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>23</sup>מ֘וֹכִ֤יחַ אָדָ֣ם אַ֭חֲרַי חֵ֣ן יִמְצָ֑א מִֽמַּחֲלִ֥יק לָשֽׁוֹן׃ <sup>24</sup>גּוֹזֵ֤ל ׀ אָ֘בִ֤יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ וְאֹמֵ֥ר אֵֽין־פָּ֑שַׁע חָבֵ֥ר ה֝֗וּא לְאִ֣ישׁ מַשְׁחִֽית׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him. <sup>18</sup>Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once. <sup>19</sup>He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough. <sup>20</sup>A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent. <sup>21</sup>To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress. <sup>22</sup>He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him. <sup>23</sup>He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue. <sup>24</sup>Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>רְחַב־נֶ֭פֶשׁ יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ עַל־יְהוָ֣ה יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃ <sup>26</sup>בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭לִבּוֹ ה֣וּא כְסִ֑יל וְהוֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּ֝חָכְמָ֗ה ה֣וּא יִמָּלֵֽט׃ <sup>27</sup>נוֹתֵ֣ן לָ֭רָשׁ אֵ֣ין מַחְס֑וֹר וּמַעְלִ֥ים עֵ֝ינָ֗יו רַב־מְאֵרֽוֹת׃ <sup>28</sup>בְּק֣וּם רְ֭שָׁעִים יִסָּתֵ֣ר אָדָ֑ם וּ֝בְאָבְדָ֗ם יִרְבּ֥וּ צַדִּיקִֽים׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat. <sup>26</sup>He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered. <sup>27</sup>He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse. <sup>28</sup>When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
